strings.name: Margaret Atwood
strings.role: Novelist and poet · Power, gender and the environment
strings.summary: Atwood writes poetry, fiction and literary criticism, often linking women’s experiences with Canadian society and ecological danger. The Handmaid’s Tale depicts political control of bodies and language; The Blind Assassin uses layered storytelling to examine memory and class. A two-time Booker winner, she also explores technology and the environment in Oryx and Crake. Her later memoir revisits the experiences behind her writing.

strings.influence.rationale: Explored power, gender and ecology in works including The Handmaid's Tale and The Blind Assassin, influencing literature and public cultural debate.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Power over bodies
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: The Handmaid’s Tale and The Testaments use an imagined society to explore gendered power, oppression and testimony.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Two Booker Prizes
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: The Blind Assassin won in 2000; The Testaments shared the 2019 Booker Prize.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Memoir interview airs
strings.timeline.event-01.text: In a WBUR interview about Book of Lives, she discussed childhood, education and the transformation of experience into fiction.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Publishes Book of Lives
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Her memoir traces upbringing, relationships and a literary career through the people and experiences behind her books.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: The Testaments shares the Booker Prize
strings.timeline.event-03.text: She returned to the society of The Handmaid’s Tale through multiple witnesses, sharing the Booker with Bernardine Evaristo.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Publishes Oryx and Crake
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The novel explores biotechnology and ecological catastrophe, beginning the fictional world of the MaddAddam trilogy.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: The Blind Assassin wins the Booker
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Interwoven memoir, family history and fiction within fiction examine class, women’s circumstances and concealed history.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Publishes The Handmaid’s Tale
strings.timeline.event-06.text: The novel imagines a regime controlling women through religion and reproductive policy, later reaching broader audiences through adaptations.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Publishes The Edible Woman
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Her first novel examines work, consumption and expectations of marriage, establishing lasting concerns with bodies and social rules.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Graduates and publishes her first poetry book
strings.timeline.event-08.text: She completed her Toronto BA and published Double Persephone before undertaking graduate study at Radcliffe.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Ottawa
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in Canada, she spent childhood between northern forests and cities; nature and reading became important contexts for her writing.
